title: Durable Response to Vebreltinib in Heavily Pretreated MET-Amplified Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Background MET amplification, although detected in only 2% to 5% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas (ICC), represents an actionable oncogenic driver. Treatment options after failure of first-line immunochemotherapy remain limited, and clinical data on vebreltinib, a novel highly selective MET inhibitor, in this molecular subset are scarce. Case presentation A 61-year-old woman with metastatic ICC harboring high-level MET amplification (tissue gene copy number, 26.79) experienced disease progression on first-line durvalumab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, second-line liposomal irinotecan/fluorouracil plus lenvatinib and durvalumab, radiotherapy, and transarterial chemoembolization. Following a brief period of vebreltinib (200 mg twice daily) plus durvalumab that was interrupted by grade 4 myelosuppression, the patient continued on vebreltinib monotherapy after hematologic recovery. Restaging computed tomography demonstrated a partial response (PR), with carbohydrate antigen 19-9 normalizing (a 99.2% reduction). This response lasted over six months until eventual disease progression. Conclusion To our knowledge, this is the first report of vebreltinib monotherapy inducing a deep and durable partial response in heavily pretreated, MET-amplified ICC, with the response lasting over six months despite eventual disease progression. This case underscores the critical value of comprehensive molecular profiling after first-line treatment failure to identify actionable drivers such as MET amplification.

title: Preoperative ultrasound in pediatric supracondylar fracture-related nerve injuries: intraoperative correlation in a tertiary referral retrospective case series.
abstract: Nerve palsy is a recognized complication of paediatric supracondylar humeral fractures. Most injuries recover spontaneously, a subset require surgical exploration, and identifying those who may benefit from intervention remains challenging. High-resolution ultrasound has emerged as a potential adjunct for assessing nerve injury, although its utility in this setting remains incompletely defined. A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary peripheral nerve injury center. Children less than 16 years with persistent supracondylar fracture-related nerve palsy who underwent preoperative ultrasound and surgical exploration between 2018 and 2024 were included. Ultrasound findings were categorized as structural abnormality, compression/tethering, neuroma/swelling, or entrapment and were compared with intraoperative findings. Analysis was descriptive, focusing on ultrasound detection of nerve abnormality and concordance with surgical findings. Twenty-two patients were included (mean age: 7 years). All had surgically confirmed nerve pathology. Ultrasound demonstrated nerve abnormality in 21 out of 22 cases (95%). Compression/tethering was the most common finding (18/22), followed by structural abnormality (14/22), neuroma/swelling (7/22), and entrapment (2/22). Intraoperatively, structural abnormalities were identified in 17 cases, compression/tethering in 21, neuroma in 3, and entrapment in 4. Ultrasound frequently identified nerve abnormality but demonstrated variable concordance with intraoperative findings, including overestimation of neuroma (7 vs. 3 cases) and under-detection of entrapment (2 vs. 4 cases). Preoperative ultrasound frequently demonstrated abnormal nerve features in children with persistent palsy following supracondylar humeral fracture. However, its limited concordance in characterizing specific pathology restricts its role as a standalone decision-making tool. Ultrasound findings should be interpreted alongside clinical assessment when considering surgical exploration.

title: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium in adolescent athletes with acute groin pain: clinical and MRI features of a radiograph-occult injury pattern.
abstract: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is an uncommon MRI finding in young athletes with acute groin pain and is frequently occult on plain radiographs. This study aimed to characterize its clinical presentation, MRI findings, associated injuries, and return-to-sport outcomes. This retrospective single-center case series included athletes aged ≤22 years who underwent MRI for acute sports-related groin pain with negative or inconclusive radiographs between 2017 and 2025. Patients meeting predefined MRI criteria for subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium were identified, and clinical, imaging, and outcome data were analyzed descriptively. Twenty of 91 patients (22.0%) met the MRI criteria. Their mean age was 13.9 ± 1.5 years, 19 (95%) were male, and 18 (90%) had open physes. Periosteal elevation was present in all patients, and 19 (95%) demonstrated a predominantly subperiosteal fluid collection, most commonly with a lentiform configuration. Associated anterior inferior iliac spine avulsion injury or intramuscular iliacus injury was identified in 10 patients (50%). All patients were managed nonoperatively and returned to unrestricted sports participation after progressive rehabilitation at a mean of 4.5 ± 2.2 weeks. Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is a reproducible MRI finding in predominantly skeletally immature athletes with acute sports-related groin pain and negative or inconclusive radiographs. Recognition of periosteal elevation with a predominantly subperiosteal fluid collection may facilitate diagnosis of this radiograph-occult injury pattern. Although the underlying injury mechanism remains hypothetical, prospective studies are needed to clarify its clinical significance.

title: Relationship between extent of jeopardized myocardium derived from myocardial viability study to post-myocardial infarction outcome.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to assess the relationship between the extent of jeopardized myocardium, quantified using cardiac viability imaging, and clinical outcomes in patients after myocardial infarction. By utilizing rest myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) and cardiac 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) analyzed with Emory Cardiac Toolbox software (ECTb), the study aimed to determine how quantitative viability parameters correlate with left ventricular functional recovery and post-myocardial infarction outcomes, and to assess their utility in guiding clinical decision-making. Methods This prospective study included 85 patients who underwent 2-day rest MPI followed by cardiac FDG-PET/CT imaging. Quantitative parameters, including the percentage of jeopardized myocardium, comprising viable, scarred, and total jeopardized myocardial segments, along with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were obtained using the ECTb platform (version 4.2). The relationship between these quantitative PET parameters and functional myocardial recovery, defined as improvement in ≥5% LVEF as assessed by two-dimensional echocardiography, was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Follow-up was conducted over a period of 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year to assess the association between baseline quantitative imaging parameters and the occurrence of adverse cardiac events. Results The analysis demonstrated that the extent of viable myocardium was a strong predictor of functional recovery (area under the curve, 0.762; P < 0.001), with a cutoff of approximately 17% yielding 76.7% sensitivity, 68.8% specificity, and 71.8% accuracy. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) occurred in 16% of patients. There was no significant association with imaging parameters, except a nonsignificant trend for scar burden in medically managed patients. Patients undergoing surgical intervention had a significantly greater extent of jeopardized myocardium, underscoring the role of viability imaging in therapeutic decision-making. Conclusion The extent of viable myocardium identified through imaging was strongly correlated with functional recovery, as reflected by improvements in cardiac function on follow-up echocardiography. Although no significant relationship with MACE was seen in the overall cohort, the higher burden of jeopardized myocardium in surgically treated patients underscores the value of viability imaging in guiding revascularization decisions, supporting FDG-PET/CT as a useful tool for post-myocardial infarction risk stratification and management.

title: The impact and value of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management of patients with cervical cancer with service evaluation audited against national evidence-based PET-CT guidelines.
abstract: Purpose First, to assess the diagnostic value of fluorine-18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET-computed tomography ([18F]-FDG PET-CT) compared with conventional MRI and/or CT. Second, to audit the clinical indications for referring patients with cervical cancer for [18F]-FDG PET-CT against the 2022 guidelines published by the Royal College of Radiologists and the Royal College of Physicians. Finally, to evaluate the impact of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management plans. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 49 patients with histologically proven cervical cancer across the Sussex Cancer Network underwent 59 [18F]-FDG PET-CT between 1 November 2020 and 31 October 2022. Scans were compared with the most recent CT and MRI scan conducted within 4 months of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT. Scan indications were categorized as either 'in accordance' or 'outside' the guidelines. Those in accordance fell into one of four groups: staging, response assessment, suspected recurrence, or staging when considering exenterative surgery. A questionnaire investigating the impact of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT on the management plan of each patient was answered by one clinical oncology consultant. Results [18F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guidelines. The management plan was changed by 5/59 scans (8.4%), confirmed by 48/59 (81.4%) and was not impacted with 6/59 (10.2%) scans. Conclusion [18F]-FDG PET-CT is superior to conventional imaging and enhances the management plan. Future cohort studies with larger patient numbers involving multicentric studies are needed to fully assess its impact on cervical cancer management and prognosis.

title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
abstract: The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.

title: Towards Medical Image Dataset Distillation: A Progressive Trajectory Matching and Dynamic Diversity Enhancing Method.
abstract: Sharing medical image sets is essential yet challenging due to limited resource and strict regulatory, which significantly hinder the development of medical foundation models and the transfer of medical domain knowledge. In this paper, we utilize medical image dataset distillation techniques to enable effective model construction and knowledge transfer without requiring downstream users to directly access the original data. Trajectory matching has become the mainstream distillation technique, yet our empirical findings on medical image datasets reveal two critical phenomena: instability of distillation optimization and redundancy of synthetic images. To investigate these phenomena, we conduct a theoretical analysis from the perspectives of bi-level optimization and neural tangent kernel, and formally define them as two core challenges: trajectory matching drift and intra-class diversity decay, which underscore the need for more stable and diversity-preserving trajectory matching methods. Guided by the analysis results, we propose a novel progressive and diverse dataset distillation (PD$^{3}$) method, which incorporates (1) a progressive trajectory matching paradigm that progressively unrolls the student training trajectory to extend the matching horizon, while adaptively selecting optimal expert matching trajectory to ensure stable and convergent distillation optimization; and (2) a dynamic diversity enhancing module that alleviates the redundancy of synthetic images by enhancing intra-class distribution and breaking redundancy accumulation. To facilitate fair evaluation, we establish a comprehensive medical image dataset distillation benchmark covering diverse medical image modalities. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves an average absolute improvement of 10.20% and a relative gain of 20.09% over prior state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its effectiveness and practical potential.

title: Association Between Local Factors and Implant-Related Complications: A Population-Sampled Cross-Sectional Analysis.
abstract: Aim To investigate the role of local factors and the association with peri-implantitis and peri-implant soft-tissue dehiscence (PISTD). Materials and methods A randomly selected sample of Norwegian patients who underwent implant therapy in 2014 was examined (242 patients; 732 implants). Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded, including soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, connection type, platform switching, emergence angle, implant location and presence of adjacent teeth. To account for clustering of implants within patients, mixed-effects logistic regression models were applied. Results Mucosal margin mobility, bone-level implants without platform switching, emergence angle > 45°, anterior implant location and daily smoking were identified as significant risk indicators for peri-implantitis. title: Experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis and management of early-stage nail unit melanoma.
abstract: Background Nail unit melanoma (NUM) is a distinct form of melanoma that most often arises from the nail matrix. No recommendations as to the management of nail melanoma, particularly of early-stage melanoma (in situ, stage IA, IB), exist. Objectives To provide practical, experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis, differential diagnosis and management of early-stage NUM, developed by an international expert panel. Methods Based on clinical and histopathological experience and an extensive literature search, the authors present recommendations for the management of patients with lesions suspicious for NUM. Results Clinically, most cases present as a longitudinal pigmented band in an adult nail. It represents 1.5-2.5% of all melanomas in Caucasians but up to 50% in Black patients. Considering that the nail unit surface area accounts for less than 1% of the total body surface, the nail matrix can be regarded as a hotspot for melanoma development. Early diagnosis is critical, as treatment at the in situ or minimally invasive stage is associated with high cure rates. While dermoscopy is a useful diagnostic aid, nail matrix biopsy with histopathology remains the gold standard. Laboratory tests and standard imaging studies are not diagnostic; however, they may assist in surgical planning for advanced cases. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice. Wide local excision is recommended for early-stage disease, with specific margins (6 mm for standard lesions; 10 mm in the presence of the Hutchinson sign). Amputation is generally reserved for thicker tumours (>1 mm). A 10-year follow-up period is recommended to monitor for potential recurrence. Conclusions Early diagnosis and treatment of nail unit melanoma at the in situ or minimally invasive stage (IA/IB) are associated with high cure rates. In contrast, advanced disease with deep invasion or metastasis carries a poor prognosis-therefore, timely recognition and intervention are essential to optimize outcomes.

title: A Case Report of a Complete Removable Denture Designed to Restore Function in a Patient With Severe Resorption of the Mandibular Alveolar Ridge Using the Neutral Zone and Flange Techniques.
abstract: Edentulous patients with severe mandibular alveolar ridge resorption struggle with denture stability, which often reduces their quality of life due to mucosal pain and food debris retention. When the inferior alveolar canal is extremely close to the alveolar crest, conventional dentures risk causing severe pain and sensory abnormalities by compressing the inferior alveolar nerve. Thus, conventional fabrication methods face clinical limitations. To stabilize a mandibular complete denture in such cases, it is highly effective to record the dynamics of the denture space and fabricate a prosthesis that harmonizes with these perioral muscle movements. A 77-year-old woman presented with frequent stomatitis caused by ill-fitting dentures and severe masticatory dysfunction. Intraoral and radiographic examinations revealed marked resorption of the mandibular alveolar ridge, placing the inferior alveolar canal in extreme proximity to the alveolar crest. The treatment plan involved fabricating a new maxillary partial denture that strictly balanced the support of the remaining teeth. For the mandible, a complete denture was fabricated using the neutral zone and flange techniques to harmonize with surrounding soft tissue movements. This approach enabled functional contouring by leveraging the dynamic pressure of the perioral muscles. Consequently, denture retention and stability improved dramatically, and denture displacement during speech was successfully suppressed. An evaluation of masticatory function confirmed objective functional recovery. This case demonstrates that for patients with severe alveolar ridge resorption and diminished anatomical supporting tissues, determining the functional form of the denture by accounting for soft-tissue dynamics is highly effective in restoring stability and masticatory function.

title: Ovarian Yolk Sac Tumor in a 10-Year-Old Girl Following Metachronous Bilateral Mature Ovarian Teratomas.
abstract: Background Ovarian germ cell tumors are the most common ovarian malignancies in children. Because these patients have a notable risk of developing metachronous bilateral tumors or recurrences, maximizing the preservation of ovarian tissue during initial surgery is critical to protecting future fertility and endocrine function. Objective A previously healthy 8-year-old girl underwent emergency laparotomy for ovarian torsion, resulting the right oophorectomy, with histopathology confirming a mature teratoma. Sixteen months later, a contralateral ovarian mass was detected and treated with ovarian-sparing excision, also diagnosed as a mature teratoma. At age 10 (10 months after the second excision), she was found to have an 8 cm pelvic tumor and elevated α -fetoprotein. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed complex solid and cystic components suggestive of a malignant germ cell tumor, with no metastases on computed tomography/MRI. The mass was removed intact at exploratory laparotomy, yielding a diagnosis of Fédération Internationale de Gynécologie et d'Obstétrique (FIGO) Stage 1A ovarian yolk sac tumor. She was discharged after completing combination chemotherapy. Currently, she is 16 years old and being managed with hormone replacement therapy. Conclusions The presented case highlights a disadvantage of overzealous oophorectomy. Detorsion of the seemingly necrotic ovary followed by second-look surgery could have preserved some ovarian function.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
abstract: Introduction Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear. Methods This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint. Results Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group. Conclusions In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

title: Impact of <sup>18</sup>FDG-Avidity and Immunosuppression on Idiopathic and Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
abstract: Background Myocardial 18 fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 FDG)-avidity is frequently seen in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy, as well as a growing "idiopathic 18 FDG-avidity" group of genotype-negative patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis. The prognostic implications of 18 FDG-avidity in patients with and without genetic cardiomyopathy, and the effects of immunosuppression in the latter, remain uncertain. Methods This multicenter, retrospective study included all patients who were referred for both 18 FDG-PET and cardiomyopathy genetic testing. Patients with acute myocarditis, biopsy-proven sarcoidosis, or extracardiac 18 FDG-avidity were excluded. We investigated heart failure (HF) composite (left ventricular assist device, heart transplant, HF hospitalization, or death) and arrhythmia composite (sustained ventricular arrhythmias [ventricular tachycardia/VF], atrioventricular block, or death) outcomes using survival analysis, including Cox proportional hazards modeling and inverse probability of treatment weighting. Results Among 372 patients, 142 (38%) were 18 FDG-avid. The prevalence of genetic cardiomyopathy among 18 FDG-avid patients (12%) was similar to that of 18 FDG-negative patients (18%; P =0.11). Unadjusted, 18 FDG-avidity was associated with an increased risk of HF composite (hazard ratio, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.04-2.75]; P =0.034) and arrhythmia composite (hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.1-2.4]; P =0.014) outcomes compared with 18 FDG-negative patients. However, these associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, nor were there significant differences in 18 FDG-associated risks in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy versus genotype-negative patients. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, immunosuppression of 18 FDG-avid patients (n=49) was not associated with a reduction in HF or arrhythmia composite outcomes compared with those who were not immunosuppressed (n=93). Conclusions Myocardial-only 18 FDG-avidity is not significantly associated with HF or arrhythmia risk in patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis (including those with genetic cardiomyopathy). Immunosuppression therapy does not seem to modify the disease course, suggesting that not all myocardial 18 FDG uptake reflects clinically significant inflammation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Across the Surgical Research Workflow: A Stage-Specific Framework for Benefits, Failure Modes, and Oversight.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly large language models (LLMs), have rapidly integrated into surgical and biomedical research, prompting fundamental questions about their appropriate role. This review presents a stage-specific framework mapping each phase of the surgical research workflow (literature review, data analysis, manuscript preparation, and research synthesis) to the role AI plays, the benefits it provides, the failure modes it introduces, and the oversight it requires. Artificial intelligence-powered query systems are designed to speed literature synthesis across thousands of publications. In data analysis, LLMs paired with statistical environments can perform regression modeling and generate auditable code, while specialized architectures support automated image segmentation and histopathology analysis. Each stage's benefits, however, are matched by characteristic failure modes: LLMs are prone to error and hallucination, reproducibility is threatened by model versioning and run-to-run variability, fabricated citations and paper-mill submissions endanger the integrity of the literature, and over-reliance risks eroding trainee competencies in critical appraisal and biostatistical reasoning. Because these failure modes are stage-specific, governance must be stage-specific as well: the framework pairs each risk with a matched oversight mechanism, and these mechanisms translate into practical implementation recommendations for surgical departments, residency programs, research groups, and journals. The integration of AI into surgical scholarship should be viewed as augmentation rather than replacement, supported by standardized disclosure frameworks, AI literacy in graduate medical education, and institutional governance structures that preserve the integrity of surgical research.

title: Limb Body Wall Complex: Report of a Discordant Case in a Monozygotic Twin Pregnancy.
abstract: Limb Body Wall Complex (LBWC) is a rare, severe congenital malformation syndrome characterized by thoracoabdominal wall defects, craniofacial anomalies, and limb and spinal malformations. Its incidence ranges from 0.04 to 3.3 per 10,000 births. We present a case of LBWC diagnosed in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy at 17 weeks of gestation. The mother was 28-year-old, primigravida, and had no notable medical history. Ultrasound identified abnormal positioning of 1 embryo, suggestive of adherence to the amnion. First-trimester scans revealed increased nuchal translucency and foot malposition in fetus A, while fetus B showed a cystic hygroma along with significant abdominal wall and spinal anomalies. Selective termination of fetus B was performed at 17 weeks but was complicated by the intrauterine demise of both fetuses. Postmortem examination of fetus B confirmed classical LBWC features: abdominopelvic wall defect with evisceration adherent to the placenta, lower limb amyotrophy, severe kyphoscoliosis, and craniofacial abnormalities. The pathogenesis of LBWC remains unclear, with hypotheses including early amnion rupture, vascular disruptions, and embryonic developmental errors. Diagnosis is typically made by prenatal ultrasound in the first trimester. LBWC is generally lethal, warranting pregnancy termination. While multiple pregnancies may increase the risk, discordant presentation in monochorionic twins remains exceptionally rare.

title: Emerging hydrogel platforms for disease modeling, diagnosis, and imaging of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the presence of amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, neurodegeneration, cognitive decline, and dementia. The exact pathogenesis is not well understood, as appropriate pathological and therapeutically relevant disease models remain limited. Hydrogels are hydrophilic, three-dimensional (3D) polymer networks composed of synthetic or natural materials and have diverse neuroscience applications, including drug delivery, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. Currently, hydrogel in vitro platforms are becoming increasingly explored for AD pathogenesis, as brain extracellular matrix-mimicking biodegradable components, for delivery of growth factors for neurons and other brain cells, AD-specific peptide release, engineered multi-region brain organoids, and therapeutic drug delivery. Beyond disease modeling, hydrogels are being used to evaluate emerging AD diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, such as biomarker sensing and the integration of imaging. Recent AD diagnostic platforms have leveraged hydrogels as biomolecule-capture matrices and signal-transduction elements to detect AD-associated biomarkers via minimally invasive or implantable systems. Hydrogels have also been harnessed in magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography imaging modalities to support imageable vehicles for therapeutic delivery. Such platforms hold promise for bridging physiologically relevant neurobiological investigation with more accessible, efficient clinical tools for AD. This review highlights recent advances in hydrogel-based disease models, diagnostic tools, and imaging technologies and their potential to integrate with brain organoids, artificial intelligence, and 3D printing to enhance mechanistic and translational applications for AD.

title: Development of <sup>99m</sup>Tc-cefadroxil loaded chitosan nanoparticles as a novel radiotracer for detection of septic and aseptic foci.
abstract: Early detection of inflammation is critical for preventing disease progression, and nuclear medicine plays a pivotal role in this context. Imaging modalities such as single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) enable the early identification of functional abnormalities through the use of targeted radiotracers that specifically localize inflammatory processes. In this regard, antibiotic-loaded nanoparticles have emerged as a promising platform for inflammation imaging, integrating diagnostic capabilities with potential therapeutic functionality. Among these systems, chitosan-based nanocarriers (CS-NPs), a nano-polymeric pharmaceutical excipient, were employed for the encapsulation of the antibiotic cefadroxil (CDX). The formulation was prepared via a simple ionic gelation (cross-linking) technique. The physicochemical properties of the resulting nanoparticles were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), zeta potential analysis, and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Drug encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were subsequently quantified by UV-visible spectrophotometry. For imaging applications, CDX-loaded CS-NPs (400 µg) were radiolabeled with technetium-99m in the presence of stannous chloride (50 µg) as a reducing agent, yielding a complex with a radiochemical efficiency of 94 ± 1.3%. The resulting 99mTc-CDX-CS-NPs demonstrated excellent in vitro stability in fresh serum for up to 6 hours, which is suitable for diagnostic imaging applications. In vivo biodistribution studies in murine models of both septic and aseptic inflammation revealed significant tracer accumulation at infected and inflamed sites, with high target-to-non-target (T/NT) ratios of 8.55 and 6.02 after 2 hours post-injection, respectively. These findings suggest the developed radiotracer's ability to effectually localize septic and aseptic foci, irrespective of their underlying etiology.

title: Reproducibility and diagnostic performance of ADC for assessing response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multi-ROI comparison analysis from the phase-Ib NABUCCO trial.
abstract: Objective MRI is increasingly used to assess treatment response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), but only qualitatively. This study evaluates the reproducibility and predictive value of quantitative apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), thought to be a non-invasive surrogate for tumor cell density, in patients with MIBC receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy. Materials and methods MRI data from 35 patients, enrolled in the Phase-Ib NABUCCO trial, were analyzed. ADC maps were derived from pre- and post-treatment MRI scans. Three independent radiologists assessed multiple regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate inter-observer agreement and predictive performance for pathological complete response (pCR). ADC values were normalized using muscle tissue as a reference. Additionally, we analyzed the correlation between ADC and cell densities, derived from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) data. Results ADC measurements from the whole-tumor ROI (n = 25) demonstrated the highest reproducibility (0.98, 95% CI = [0.95-0.99]), but lacked predictive value (AUC = 0.31, 95% CI = [0.12-0.53], p = 0.109). The most hypointense ROI (n = 22) showed the strongest predictive value for pCR (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.57-1], p = 0.025), though with limited reproducibility. The difference between baseline and follow-up ADC values in the hypointense region (n = 20) again showed the highest diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.58-0.98], p = 0.015). Although muscle normalization is proposed to reduce scanner variability, it did not improve predictive performance in this cohort and occasionally reduced reproducibility. No significant correlation was found between whole-tumor ADC and cell density. Conclusion Despite analyzing different measurement techniques for ADC values, none was simultaneously reproducible and predictive, nor provided insights into the biology of the tumor. While ADC shows promise in MIBC, there is an urgent need for more standardized, robust imaging biomarkers. Key points Question Non-invasive biomarkers are urgently needed to guide bladder-preserving strategies in MIBC. Findings DWI-MRI shows promise, but standardized robust imaging biomarkers are essential for reliable response assessment. Critical relevance statement Standardized or AI-assisted ROI segmentation could improve ADC reproducibility and diagnostic accuracy in multicenter studies.

title: Optimizing AI-assisted decision-making in mammography screening: focusing on uncertainties.
abstract: Objective To evaluate an AI-based decision-support system for mammography interpretation, assessing its impact on diagnostic performance. Materials and methods This retrospective study analyzed 130,838 mammograms from 35,709 patients with confirmed follow-up outcomes across multiple centers, using the Digital Database for Screening Mammography (DDSM) for external validation. Representing one of the largest datasets from the Middle East, it evaluates model generalizability in underrepresented populations. An AI super-model incorporated separate UNet-based networks for lesion segmentation, a high-resolution model (4096) for calcifications, a multi-resolution ensemble (4096, 2048, 1024) for macro-scale lesions, and a risk-assessment model for malignancy prediction. Radiologists interpreted images under five scenarios: unaided, AI-assisted, AI as the final decision-maker in uncertain cases, union of radiologist and AI decisions in uncertain cases, and standalone AI. Results AI assistance significantly enhanced performance across all scenarios. Based on aggregated reader performance, AUC improved from 83.04% (95% CI: 79.8-86.3) unaided to 88.40% (95% CI: 85.6-91.2) in the union scenario (p < 0.001). Sensitivity increased from 54.8% (95% CI: 48.6-61.0) to 83.9% (95% CI: 79.3-88.4) (p < 0.001), and specificity rose from 83.6% (95% CI: 82.0-85.3) to 91.1% (95% CI: 89.8-92.4) (p < 0.001). Multi-resolution segmentation effectively detected calcifications and challenging lesions. DDSM validation confirmed model robustness. AI showed particular promise in aiding less-experienced radiologists in underserved areas to improve early cancer detection. Conclusions AI in mammography interpretation improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces uncertainty, supporting early breast cancer detection and optimized screening workflows. Key points Question Can an AI-based decision-support system improve the accuracy of mammography interpretation, reduce diagnostic uncertainty, and support less-experienced radiologists? Findings In this retrospective multicenter study, AI-assisted mammography improved sensitivity and specificity, increased cancer detection, and reduced recalls and false positives. Critical relevance statement AI integration in mammography enhances diagnostic accuracy, reduces unnecessary recalls, and supports more confident and efficient clinical decision-making, particularly by improving the performance of less-experienced radiologists in underserved and resource-limited settings where expert interpretation may be limited.

An AI super-model incorporated separate UNet-based networks for lesion segmentation, a high-resolution model (4096) for calcifications, a multi-resolution ensemble (4096, 2048, 1024) for macro-scale lesions, and a risk-assessment model for malignancy prediction. Radiologists interpreted images under five scenarios: unaided, AI-assisted, AI as the final decision-maker in uncertain cases, union of radiologist and AI decisions in uncertain cases, and standalone AI.

Results

AI assistance significantly enhanced performance across all scenarios. Based on aggregated reader performance, AUC improved from 83.04% (95% CI: 79.8-86.3) unaided to 88.40% (95% CI: 85.6-91.2) in the union scenario (p < 0.001). Sensitivity increased from 54.8% (95% CI: 48.6-61.0) to 83.9% (95% CI: 79.3-88.4) (p < 0.001), and specificity rose from 83.6% (95% CI: 82.0-85.3) to 91.1% (95% CI: 89.8-92.4) (p < 0.001). Multi-resolution segmentation effectively detected calcifications and challenging lesions. DDSM validation confirmed model robustness. AI showed particular promise in aiding less-experienced radiologists in underserved areas to improve early cancer detection.

Conclusions

AI in mammography interpretation improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces uncertainty, supporting early breast cancer detection and optimized screening workflows.

Key points

Question Can an AI-based decision-support system improve the accuracy of mammography interpretation, reduce diagnostic uncertainty, and support less-experienced radiologists? Findings In this retrospective multicenter study, AI-assisted mammography improved sensitivity and specificity, increased cancer detection, and reduced recalls and false positives. Critical relevance statement AI integration in mammography enhances diagnostic accuracy, reduces unnecessary recalls, and supports more confident and efficient clinical decision-making, particularly by improving the performance of less-experienced radiologists in underserved and resource-limited settings where expert interpretation may be limited.

title: Impact of deep learning image reconstruction on CT radiomics reproducibility in patients with pulmonary nodules.
abstract: Objective Ensuring CT feature reproducibility across imaging protocols and reconstruction algorithms is essential for the generalizability of radiomics applications. This study aimed to evaluate the reproducibility of CT radiomic features in pulmonary nodules using deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) compared with conventional reconstruction techniques under different radiation doses. Materials and methods We included 94 patients between March and June 2023. Standard- and low-dose CT images were scanned to assess the impact of dose reduction on feature reproducibility. DLIR strengths at low (DLIR-L), medium (DLIR-M), and high (DLIR-H), representing progressive levels of noise suppression, were compared against filtered back projection (FBP) and adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V at 50% strength (ASIR-V-50%) reconstructions. 2264 features were extracted from pulmonary nodules. The concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and the coefficient of variation (CV) were used to evaluate inter-dose reproducibility, inter-reconstruction reproducibility, and feature variability. Results The mean CCC for inter-dose reproducibility using DLIR-H, ASIR-V-50%, and FBP was 0.934 ± 0.104, 0.922 ± 0.128, and 0.922 ± 0.113, respectively (p = 0.055), with 29.8%, 27.9%, and 20.2% of features showing near-perfect agreement. In low-dose CT, DLIR-L achieved the highest inter-reconstruction reproducibility against ASIR-V-50% (0.950 ± 0.094), with 39.4% of features showing near-perfect agreement. The overall CV across reconstructions was 9.87 ± 20.32%, with 74.0% of features highly stable. Part-solid nodules showed the lowest variability (7.17 ± 13.48%, p < 0.001). Reproducibility improved significantly with increasing nodule size (p < 0.001). Conclusion DLIR improves the radiomic feature reproducibility in pulmonary nodules, making it particularly suitable for low-dose CT protocols. However, the robustness tends to decrease with higher DLIR strengths. Nodule characteristics significantly influence variability. Key points Question The impact of DLIR on radiomic feature reproducibility across radiation doses and reconstruction methods in pulmonary nodules remains unknown. Findings DLIR-H demonstrated high inter-dose reproducibility, while DLIR-L achieved the highest inter-reconstruction reproducibility; feature variability decreased significantly with increasing nodule size, with 21 robust features identified. Critical relevance statementThis study critically assesses reconstruction-related instability in CT radiomics and identifies DLIR settings and nodule characteristics that influence feature robustness, supporting protocol optimization and more reliable quantitative pulmonary nodule assessment in clinical radiology.

title: Ultrasonography in disaster medicine: a narrative review.
abstract: This narrative review aimed to critically appraise the diagnostic accuracy, clinical impact, and operational feasibility of ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) across the four domains of disaster medicine. A literature search was conducted following the SANRA and PRISMA-trAIce guidelines. Records were identified through an AI-assisted literature-discovery tool (the Undermind Deep-Search platform, interrogating the Semantic Scholar corpus) run on 15 June 2025, rather than through an independent structured multi-database search. Candidate references were screened manually against pre-specified eligibility criteria by a single reviewer, with the search parameters independently verified by the senior author. Of 71 records identified, 63 met the inclusion criteria. The included studies comprised 32 original studies, 10 systematic or scoping reviews, 20 narrative or operational papers, and one guideline. In CBRN scenarios, lung ultrasound demonstrated sensitivities of 90-97% for COVID-19 pneumonia versus 60-69% for chest radiography while minimizing healthcare worker exposure. For blast and ballistic injuries, FAST showed a pooled sensitivity of 92.1% (95% CI: 87.8-95.6) and specificity of 98.7% (95% CI: 96.0-99.9) for intra-abdominal hemorrhage. In natural disasters, ultrasound altered management in up to 44% of patients. Post-disaster applications included vascular access, tube confirmation, and complication monitoring. Ultraportable POCUS demonstrates diagnostic utility and operational feasibility across multiple disaster domains. However, evidence quality varies significantly, and standardized protocols remain lacking. Prospective studies linking ultrasound deployment to improved patient outcomes are needed. KEY POINTS: Question When disasters disable conventional imaging, how does ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography perform for diagnosis, triage, and procedural guidance across the four domains of disaster medicine? Findings Across 63 studies, FAST reached 92.1% pooled sensitivity for hemoperitoneum, lung ultrasound 90-97% versus 60-69% for radiography; management changed in up to 44%. Critical relevance statement This review critically appraises ultraportable ultrasound across all four disaster domains, showing that radiation-free bedside imaging accelerates triage, conserves scarce CT capacity, and extends radiological expertise through tele-guidance, while exposing an evidence base still lacking prospective outcome data.

title: MRI for restaging pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is a tumor with a dismal prognosis, as the majority of patients are diagnosed when the tumor is not resectable. Neoadjuvant treatment has significantly improved prognosis, but assessing treatment response can be challenging for radiologists. Given the fibrotic nature of the primary tumor, differentiating between residual viable tumor and fibrotic response can be difficult. MRI can have a role in reassessing the primary tumor and disease spread. In this review, we discuss MR techniques that can be used for this assessment, including routinely used sequences (e.g., DWI) and sequences that are not yet routinely included in pancreatic protocols (e.g., T1 mapping, ECV imaging, and USPIO contrast for nodal staging). KEY POINTS: Question Imaging assessment of the response of pancreatic adenocarcinoma to neoadjuvant treatment is difficult and still has limited accuracy. Findings Different MRI sequences and techniques have been suggested as possibly improving this assessment, reflecting on better patient management. Critical relevance statement We summarize the available evidence on MRI for restaging pancreatic carcinoma after neoadjuvant treatment.

title: Automated thigh muscle segmentation using foundation models: validation and impact of segmentation quality.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to validate a segmentation pipeline for the extraction of volumetric thigh muscle data, investigate the influence of demographics on segmentation performance, and investigate the influence of low-quality segmentations on quantitative performance and downstream metrics. Materials and methods Manual thigh muscle segmentations on axial T1-weighted spin echo thigh images of 364 (106 training and validation; 258 testing) participants of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) were used. A trained YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection model generated labels and box predictions, that were passed to a fine-tuned foundation model (Segment Anything, Meta), which generated muscle segmentations. The quality of segmentations was assessed by two radiologists (none, minor, major issue), and Dice scores and mean bias versus manual segmentations were calculated in the testing dataset. Linear regression was used to calculate the associations of age, sex, and BMI with Dice scores. Results Dice scores ranged between 0.97 (quadriceps) and 0.89 (adductors). Exclusion of erroneous segmentations decreased mean bias by 0.06 mL across muscle groups; mean Dice of segmentations with versus without major issues was 0.90 versus 0.94. Female sex was associated with marginally lower Dice scores (beta -0.01, 95% CI: -0.02, -0.01, p < 0.001), while no other demographic feature showed significant associations. Conclusion Foundation models can be fine-tuned on a modest task-specific dataset to achieve segmentation accuracy comparable to bespoke networks, without training a dedicated architecture from scratch. Visually erroneous segmentations introduce only negligible degradation of quantitative performance and downstream metrics and may thus be challenging to identify by data-driven detection strategies. Key points Question Foundation models can be efficiently leveraged for robust segmentation on complex thigh muscle anatomy Findings Radiologist-identified erroneous segmentations introduced only negligible degradation of summary quantitative performance and are thus difficult to identify using statistical methods. Relevance statement Human-in-the-loop quality assurance post-validation adds limited value to improve downstream volumetric muscle metrics in foundation-model-based thigh segmentation. These findings carry implications for both research and potential clinical applications of muscle volume quantification, e.g., personalized therapeutic regimens.

title: Toward Clinically Actionable Prediction of Recurrence and Metastatic Progression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Purpose Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has high rates of early recurrence (ER), occult metastasis, and poor survival despite curative-intent therapy. Predictive factors and models span clinical, biomarker, imaging, radiomics, pathologic, and molecular domains, but clinical readiness remains uncertain. Methods We performed a systematic review in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses. Five databases were searched for studies evaluating predictors or models of PDAC recurrence, metastasis, lymph node metastasis (LNM), occult metastatic disease, disease-free survival (DFS) or recurrence-free survival, or recurrence patterns. Studies were screened and coded for end point, modality, model type, validation, discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and predictor timing. Results Of 234 full-text records, 208 studies were included, comprising 144 prediction models and 64 predictor/prognostic factor studies. Computed tomography/radiomics (141/208), clinical/electronic health record variables (104/208), and serum/urine biomarkers (46/208) were the most common modalities. External validation, calibration, and decision-curve analyses were reported in 52, 36, and 38 model studies, respectively. AUCs ranged from 0.70 to 0.92 for ER, 0.75-0.95 for LNM, and 0.71-0.88 for liver or occult metastasis; DFS/relapse-free survival models had C-indices of 0.62-0.82. One externally validated occult-metastasis model had a C-statistic of 0.56. Model maturity was limited by retrospective design, heterogeneous end points, incomplete calibration reporting, and postoperative variables in preoperative models. Conclusion Prediction models for PDAC recurrence and metastatic progression are rapidly expanding, particularly through radiomics, machine learning, and multimodal modeling. Clinical translation requires decision-aligned design, transparent reporting, external validation, calibration, interpretability, and prospective evaluation of clinical utility.

Purpose

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has high rates of early recurrence (ER), occult metastasis, and poor survival despite curative-intent therapy. Predictive factors and models span clinical, biomarker, imaging, radiomics, pathologic, and molecular domains, but clinical readiness remains uncertain.

Methods

We performed a systematic review in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses. Five databases were searched for studies evaluating predictors or models of PDAC recurrence, metastasis, lymph node metastasis (LNM), occult metastatic disease, disease-free survival (DFS) or recurrence-free survival, or recurrence patterns. Studies were screened and coded for end point, modality, model type, validation, discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and predictor timing.

Results

Of 234 full-text records, 208 studies were included, comprising 144 prediction models and 64 predictor/prognostic factor studies. Computed tomography/radiomics (141/208), clinical/electronic health record variables (104/208), and serum/urine biomarkers (46/208) were the most common modalities. External validation, calibration, and decision-curve analyses were reported in 52, 36, and 38 model studies, respectively. AUCs ranged from 0.70 to 0.92 for ER, 0.75-0.95 for LNM, and 0.71-0.88 for liver or occult metastasis; DFS/relapse-free survival models had C-indices of 0.62-0.82. One externally validated occult-metastasis model had a C-statistic of 0.56. Model maturity was limited by retrospective design, heterogeneous end points, incomplete calibration reporting, and postoperative variables in preoperative models.

Conclusion

Prediction models for PDAC recurrence and metastatic progression are rapidly expanding, particularly through radiomics, machine learning, and multimodal modeling. Clinical translation requires decision-aligned design, transparent reporting, external validation, calibration, interpretability, and prospective evaluation of clinical utility.

title: Coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodule presented as adrenal incidentaloma.
abstract: Adrenal hemangiomas are rare benign vascular tumors, an uncommon cause of adrenal incidentalomas. We report a patient with coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodules within the same adrenal gland. A 67-year-old man was referred for an incidental left adrenal mass. Noncontrast computed tomography revealed a 1.6 × 1.4 cm lesion with an unenhanced attenuation value of 40 Hounsfield units. Initial hormonal evaluation was unremarkable except for an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) of 115.6. On follow-up evaluation, the ARR decreased to 52.8, with a relatively low aldosterone concentration of 9.5 ng/dL (264 pmol/L; reference range, 2.52-39.2 ng/dL [69-1087 pmol/L]), yielding equivocal findings for primary aldosteronism. Serial imaging revealed growth to 3.4 × 2.8 cm over 3 years. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a T2-hyperintense lesion with peripheral nodular enhancement and delayed centripetal filling, suggestive of adrenal hemangioma. Owing to continued growth, laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed cavernous hemangioma. Given the marked postoperative reduction in ARR to 9.7, additional pathological review identified an adjacent CYP11B2-positive aldosterone-producing micronodule. This report illustrates that adrenal incidentalomas may have dual pathologies. An integrated assessment of imaging, biochemical findings, clinical course, and histopathology, together with close clinicopathological collaboration, is essential for accurate diagnosis and management.

title: Long-term cyclic ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone syndrome with extreme fluctuations and adrenal insufficiency.
abstract: A 77-year-old woman presented with worsening glycemic control and hypokalemia and was found to have adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent hypercortisolism with loss of diurnal cortisol variation and failure of suppression on low- and high-dose dexamethasone suppression tests. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral adrenal enlargement, whereas pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and chest CT failed to identify a source of ACTH secretion, leading to a diagnosis of occult ectopic ACTH syndrome. During 15 years of follow-up, she exhibited cyclic fluctuations in ACTH and cortisol concentrations, including episodes of severe hypercortisolism with ACTH levels exceeding 2000 pg/mL (>440 pmol/L) (reference range, 7.2-63.6 pg/mL [1.6-14.0 pmol/L]) and cortisol concentrations of 30-60 μg/dL (828-1656 nmol/L) (reference range, 6.2-19.4 μg/dL [171-535 nmol/L]), alternating with spontaneous remission. Serial imaging revealed dynamic adrenal morphological changes, with enlargement during hypercortisolemic phases and regression during remission. During treatment with ketoconazole, mitotane, and osilodrostat, the patient experienced recurrent significant hypocortisolic episodes, some of which were likely treatment-associated and required hydrocortisone replacement therapy. This case highlights an exceptionally prolonged course of cyclic ectopic ACTH syndrome characterized by extreme hormonal oscillation, reversible adrenal hyperplasia, and recurrent hypocortisolism, emphasizing the importance of long-term biochemical surveillance and individualized therapeutic adjustment.

title: When anorexia nervosa conceals Cushing syndrome: a diagnostic pitfall in hypercortisolemia.
abstract: A 37-year-old woman presented with severe hypertension, mood changes, and weight loss (body mass index 14.6 kg/m 2 ). She exhibited restrictive eating behaviors consistent with anorexia nervosa, alongside biochemical hypercortisolemia with serum cortisol 43.6 µg/dL (1204 nmol/L; reference range: 6.2-18.1 µg/dL; 170-500 nmol/L), 24-hour urinary free cortisol 430.3 µg/24 hours (1187 nmol/24 hours; reference range: <60.2 µg/24 hours; <166 nmol/24 hours), and unsuppressed adrenocorticotropic hormone of 19.1 pg/mL (4.2 pmol/L; reference range: 7.3-63.1 pg/mL; 1.6-13.9 pmol/L). The cortisol level after the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test was 23.9 µg/dL (659 nmol/L; reference range: <1.8 µg/dL; <50 nmol/L). Cortisol remained markedly elevated after nasogastric feeding and weight restoration. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a 4 mm left anterior pituitary lesion. High-dose dexamethasone suppression, corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation, and inferior petrosal sinus sampling confirmed a pituitary source of adrenocorticotropic hormone. The patient underwent transsphenoidal resection of a corticotroph adenoma. Eleven months later, her hypertension and restrictive eating behaviors had resolved, and her mood significantly improved. Cushing syndrome can coexist with anorexia nervosa, masking typical cushingoid features and presenting with psychiatric manifestations and weight loss. Persistent hypercortisolemia despite nutritional rehabilitation should prompt dynamic endocrine testing and pituitary evaluation to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.

title: Calcimimetic therapy modified the radiological, surgical, and histopathological features of a parathyroid adenoma.
abstract: Calcimimetics are increasingly used to control hypercalcemia before parathyroidectomy. Although treatment-induced degenerative changes have been reported in parathyroid adenomas, their effects on preoperative imaging and surgical planning remain unclear. A 70-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism was administered preoperative evocalcet (2 mg/day). After ∼2 months, serum calcium levels decreased to the hypocalcemic range, prompting drug discontinuation before surgery referral. Upon presentation, corrected serum calcium normalized to 9.1 mg/dL (SI: 2.28 mmol/L; reference range, 8.8-10.1 mg/dL [SI: 2.20-2.53 mmol/L]), whereas intact parathyroid hormone remained mildly elevated at 65.7 pg/mL (SI: 7.0 pmol/L; reference range, 10-65 pg/mL [SI: 1.1-6.9 pmol/L]). Ultrasonography revealed a right superior parathyroid lesion, with markedly decreased Doppler flow. Four-dimensional computed tomography revealed weak enhancement throughout the contrast-enhanced phase. Parathyroidectomy revealed marked fibrosis and dense adhesions around the recurrent laryngeal nerve, making dissection technically demanding, although the nerve was preserved. Histopathological examination confirmed parathyroid adenoma with extensive fibrosis, cystic degeneration, necrosis, and macrophage infiltration. Therefore, calcimimetic therapy may modify the radiological and histopathological characteristics of parathyroid adenomas and intraoperative findings relevant to surgical planning. Recognition of these treatment-induced changes may improve the interpretation of preoperative images, help surgeons anticipate dense adhesions, and facilitate meticulous surgical dissection.

title: Primary adrenal small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in a patient with sarcoidosis and synchronous colon adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Primary adrenal neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), particularly the small cell subtype, is exceptionally rare. In patients with sarcoidosis, inflammatory lymphadenopathy may mimic a metastatic disease, making disease detection difficult. A 76-year-old man with sarcoidosis was referred for an enlarging left adrenal incidentaloma that had increased in size from 7 mm to 19 × 14 mm over 3 years. Hormonal evaluation revealed unremarkable findings; laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed because malignancy could not be excluded. Histopathological examination revealed small cell NEC with positive synaptophysin and chromogranin A staining, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 80%. One month after surgery, para-aortic lymphadenopathy was detected. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (CT) showed uptake in the para-aortic lymph nodes and ascending colon, where colonoscopy identified synchronous adenocarcinoma. The cause of the lymphadenopathy was uncertain because of coexisting sarcoidosis and colon cancer. Cisplatin plus irinotecan induced a partial response; however, disease progression was observed. CT-guided lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic NEC. Second-line amrubicin therapy reduced tumor size; comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a tumor mutation-burden-high phenotype. This case highlights diagnostic challenges in the evaluation of lymphadenopathy in patients with sarcoidosis and synchronous malignancy, emphasizing the importance of pathological confirmation for guiding appropriate management.

title: Quadriceps Strength Recovery Trajectories Associate with Pre-Operative Predictors but not Clinical Outcomes Following ACL Reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose Quadriceps weakness following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is common, however distinct longitudinal strength trajectories not have been examined. This study aimed to i) identify strength trajectories measured pre-operatively to 12 months post-ACLR, and determine associations with ii) pre-operative demographics, patient-reported outcomes (PROs: Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score [KOOS], Tegner, Marx) and ACLR concomitant surgeries, and iii) clinical outcomes post-ACLR including cartilage compositional changes (via magnetic resonance imaging [MRI] T1ρ relaxation times) and 12-month KOOS. Methods Isometric quadriceps strength was measured bilaterally pre-operatively and at 4, 6, and 12 months. Group trajectory modeling characterized longitudinal strength recovery in ACLR and uninvolved limbs, which were combined to define dual-limb recovery patterns. Tibiofemoral and patellofemoral cartilage composition was measured pre-operatively and at 12 months post-ACLR. Dirichlet regressions examined associations between trajectories and demographics, surgeries, PROs, and cartilage changes. Results 59 participants were included (58% female; age, 21.9 ± 4.7y; BMI, 24.55 ± 3.7kg/m 2). Three combined trajectories were identified: bilaterally weak (51%), which demonstrated uninvolved limb strength declines and failure to recover ACLR limb pre-operative strength; bilaterally strong (38%), which demonstrated minimal uninvolved limb declines and ACLR limb pre-operative strength recovery; and weak uninvolved, strong ACLR limb (12%). Lower pre-injury Tegner scores associated with bilaterally weak membership (p = 0.01), where probability increased from 0.27 (score of 10) to 0.61 (score of 0). Medial meniscectomy associated most with bilaterally weak membership (p<.001, 0.86 probability). No associations were found between trajectories and clinical outcomes. Conclusions While individuals who failed to restore ACLR limb strength demonstrated bilateral quadriceps weakness pre-operatively, persons who demonstrated greater pre-operative bilateral strength recovered ACLR limb strength. Medial meniscectomy associated with an inability to restore quadriceps strength.

title: Successful Kidney Transplantation Under Combined Spinal-Epidural Anesthesia in a Patient With a History of Left Pneumonectomy Due to Bronchiectasis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Kidney transplantation offers clear survival and quality-of-life advantages over dialysis, but severe pulmonary disease can complicate perioperative planning. In patients with substantially reduced respiratory reserve after pneumonectomy, general anesthesia may be considered high risk, creating uncertainty about transplant feasibility. CASE REPORT A 33-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease secondary to biopsy-proven AA amyloidosis was evaluated for preemptive living-donor kidney transplantation. He had undergone left pneumonectomy in 2015 because of bronchiectasis. Pulmonary function testing showed a mixed restrictive-obstructive pattern, with a forced vital capacity of 1.6 L (33% predicted), a forced expiratory volume in 1 second of 1.05 L (30% predicted), and a forced expiratory volume in 1 second/forced vital capacity ratio of 65%, indicating severe pulmonary impairment. Thoracic computed tomography demonstrated leftward mediastinal shift and diffuse bronchiectatic changes in the remaining right lung. Given the anticipated risk associated with general anesthesia, combined spinal-epidural anesthesia was selected. The transplant was successfully performed using a kidney from the patient's human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-identical sister. No intraoperative respiratory or hemodynamic instability occurred. Renal function rapidly improved after surgery: serum creatinine decreased from 6.6 mg/dL preoperatively to 0.63 mg/dL on postoperative day 3. Heavy proteinuria also greatly improved during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS This case demonstrates that kidney transplantation can be successfully performed under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia in carefully selected patients with severely limited pulmonary reserve after pneumonectomy. It also highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic planning and close multidisciplinary coordination for complex transplant candidates with major pulmonary comorbidities.

title: MRI-based machine learning models for differentiating Parkinson’s disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
abstract: Background: Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) are neurodegenerative disorder which have Parkinsonism as core clinical feature. PD and PSP are often misdiagnosed in early phases by conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Hence the objective of the study is to evaluate accuracy of MRI based machine learning (ML) models for differentiating PD and PSP. Methods This is a retrospective study including total of 96 subjects (32 PD, 32 PSP and 32 healthy controls). The basal nuclei region such as substantia nigra (SN), caudate nucleus (CN), putamen, globus pallidus (GP), red nucleus (RN), and subthalamic nucleus (STN) were manually segmented in T2 weighted fluid attenuation inversion recovery (T2W-FLAIR) images and radiomics features (RF) were extracted. The top 20 RF were used to train and test ML models. Performance measures of ML models for differentiating PD, PSP and HC were evaluated. Results For differentiating PD from PSP, SN consistently showed highest performance achieving accuracy, F1score and AUC values of 0.95–1.00 across all the tested ML models. RN and STN also demonstrated near perfect classification with several ML models with accuracy and AUC values of 1.00. CN, putamen and GP showed moderate performance (accuracy 38% - 85%). Among classifiers, AdaBoost provided robust performance achieving AUC up to 0.89 and MCC up to 0.72 in test data sets. Conclusion MRI based radiomics models from SN, STN and RN provide the most accurate classification of PD and PSP. It can also help in diagnosis of PD and PSP which are undifferentiable in early stages of disease.

title: Vigorous physical activity and physical function are strongly associated with better health in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the impact of physical function and level of physical activity on health status and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA). Methods In total, 141 patients with long-standing r-axSpA were included in this cross-sectional cohort study. Assessments included physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI)), spinal mobility (modified Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI)), muscle function for leg strength (Timed Stands Test (TST)) and handgrip force (Grippit), amount of self-reported physical activity (vigorous physical activity, moderate physical activity, sedentary behavior), health status by ASAS Health Index (ASAS HI) and HRQoL with Short Form Survey Instrument 36-Item. Multivariable linear regression was used to analyze associations between health status, HRQoL, physical activity, muscle function, and physical function. Results The mean (SD) age was 60 (12) years, diagnosis duration was 25 (10) years, and 57% were male. Physical function and vigorous physical activity were the strongest determinants of health status and HRQoL. The models explained approximately 50% of the variation in ASAS HI and the physical aspects of HRQoL and 21% of the mental aspects of HRQoL. Participants displayed good health status (62%) by ASAS HI ≤ 5, reached the recommended level of health-enhancing physical activity (77%), had normal muscle function (TST 82% and Grippit 91%), and demonstrated physical function (55%), and spinal mobility (45%) within reference values. Conclusion This study highlights the importance of regular vigorous physical activity in older individuals living with long-standing r-axSpA since it was strongly associated with health status and HRQoL.

title: When Imaging is Negative: Endoscopic Diagnosis of a Secondary Aortoduodenal Fistula.
abstract: Aortoenteric fistula is a life-threatening aortic graft complication with a narrow opportunity for treatment. We present a patient with aortobifemoral bypass who developed recurrent anemia and melena. Despite previous upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, computed tomography angiogram, and tagged red blood cell scan, his symptoms were persistent. Capsule endoscopy showed blood in the duodenum. Push enteroscopy revealed graft erosion in the duodenum, confirming aortoduodenal fistula. He underwent aortobifemoral graft excision, and resection of the third portion of the duodenum with end-to-side duodenojejunostomy, highlighting the importance of endoscopy in timely diagnosis of aortoenteric fistulae.

title: Pulmonary CT classification based on CNN and Grad-CAM explainability using VGG16 and MobileNetV2.
abstract: Objectives This study compared the classification performance of VGG16 and MobileNetV2 models for normal-versus-lung-cancer-positive pulmonary CT image classification, with Grad-CAM used for post-hoc visual explainability. Methods A hospital-provided dataset of 550 non-contrast thoracic CT images, comprising 240 normal and 310 lung cancer-positive images, was divided into training, validation and test subsets using a patient-grouped stratified 50/10/40 split. Images were acquired at 120 kV with a 512 × 512 matrix using a NeuViz 128 CT scanner. Both models used the same preprocessing, training-only augmentation and evaluation protocol. The VGG16 model used stacked convolutional blocks, whereas MobileNetV2 used inverted residual bottlenecks with global average pooling, dropout and a sigmoid classification layer. Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, balanced accuracy, ROC-AUC, MCC and Cohen's kappa, while Grad-CAM examined decision-relevant regions. Results On the 220-image independent test set, VGG16 achieved 0.9636 accuracy, 0.9677 sensitivity, 0.9583 specificity and 0.9569 ROC-AUC. MobileNetV2 achieved 0.9909 accuracy, 0.9919 sensitivity, 0.9896 specificity and 0.9858 ROC-AUC, with fewer false-positive and false-negative predictions. Conclusions MobileNetV2 achieved stronger held-out test performance than VGG16 under identical experimental conditions. Larger multi-centre patient-level validation remains necessary before clinical deployment in CT screening workflows.

title: Equity-aware stochastic optimization of mammography screening facility location under demand and capacity uncertainty
abstract: Abstract Uneven geographic access to mammography can limit participation in breast cancer screening, particularly in rural and underserved communities. We developed a statewide planning framework that combines geospatial accessibility analysis with stochastic facility-location optimization to identify locations for new mammography facilities under uncertainty in screening demand and existing-facility capacity. The analysis included 5.58 million Texas women aged 40–74 years, 615 existing facilities, and 222 candidate locations. The model first maximized expected screening coverage and then reduced population-weighted differences in potential access across eight race and ethnicity groups without sacrificing coverage. Opening 62 facilities across 58 counties increased expected coverage from 92.47% to 98.09% and reduced expected unmet demand from 420,089 to 106,822 women annually. Between-group variance (BGV) in access decreased by 32%, while access for the worst-served group increased from 0.858 to 0.953 effective screening slots per eligible woman. All selected locations were in baseline access-gap areas; 44% were in nonmetropolitan counties and 39% established the first mammography facility in their county. Explicitly modeling uncertainty reduced expected unmet demand by 29,643 women compared with deterministic planning. These results show that a modest, equity-aware expansion of fixed mammography capacity can substantially widen screening access and narrow both racial and geographic disparities—by placing facilities where under-served populations live rather than where volume is highest—while the most remote communities are better served by mobile screening than by additional fixed sites.

title: Robot-Tracked Multi-View 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction for Quantitative Assessment of Simulated Abdominal Haemorrhage in a Tissue-Mimicking Phantom
abstract: Abstract Background Rapid identification and assessment of abdominal haemorrhage are important in trauma. Conventional 2D US is well established for detecting free abdominal fluid but is unsuited to directly quantifying irregular fluid collections. This study established a robot-tracked multi-view 3D US framework for quantitative reconstruction of abdominal free fluid in a tissue-mimicking phantom. Methods A Philips VL13-5 3D transducer on a Philips EPIQ 7 system was rigidly mounted to a Franka Emika Panda robot. US–robot hand–eye calibration used 64 manually aligned 3D US volumes and 13-fold held-out pose cross-validation. A phantom with a controllable reservoir designed to represent free-fluid accumulation within the Morison’s pouch imaging region was imaged at 70 mL, 100 mL, 120 mL, 150 mL, and 190 mL. Two sonographers acquired 122 overlapping 3D US volumes along a two-pass trajectory. Tracking-derived reconstructions were refined using semi-automatic rigid registration and expert verification. Free fluid was manually segmented in all source volumes, and reconstructed volumes were compared with target injected-volume references. Results Final calibration achieved an RMS point-to-point reconstruction error of 1.23 mm; pooled held-out RMS error was 1.27 mm. Tracking-derived reconstruction reproduced the acquisition geometry but retained residual inter-volume misalignment and underestimated free-fluid volume, with MAPE of 9.78%. Expert-verified refinement reduced MAPE to 0.90%, with absolute relative volumetric errors of 0.07–2.61%. Conclusion Tracking provided a spatial basis for multi-view 3D US reconstruction, but accurate inter-volume registration was required for reliable volumetric quantification. The framework provides a benchmark for automated registration, segmentation, and wide-field multi-aperture ultrasound development.

title: Structured Modality Dropout for Robust MRI-Based IDH Mutation Classification in Glioma
abstract: Abstract The classification of IDH gene mutation is an essential marker in the treatment of a group of brain tumors called glioma, indicating the favorability of prognosis and response to treatment. Current methods determine the IDH mutation status invasively through postoperative tissue and DNA analysis. It is favorable to predict the mutation status non-invasively from MRI scans to determine suitable surgical strategies. Existing MRI-based prediction models often assume the availability of all four MRI modalities. However, in real-world clinical settings, one or more modalities may be missing due to reasons such as image quality and inconsistent protocols. This severely impacts the performance of MRI-based deep learning models. This study proposes a structured modality dropout training strategy to improve the robustness of a 3D ResNet18 model for IDH prediction. We compared three training strategies: Baseline (no dropout), Dropout-30 (moderate), and Dropout-50 (aggressive). All three models were evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation across six realistic modality availability scenarios (all four, missing T1CE, missing FLAIR, missing T2, T1 and T2 only, T1 only). Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, and bootstrap confidence intervals (CI). Key Findings: The Baseline model performed best when all four modalities were available (AUC $0.823 \pm 0.042$), but the Dropout models showed more stable performance as the number of missing modalities increased. The Dropout-30 model showed the best calibration, with the lowest Brier score of $0.198$. Overall, Dropout-30 was the most balanced and clinically viable model, remaining the most stable across scenarios, best calibrated, and showing good generalization across scanner models.
